_README: The Met video selection: a READING pass, not a keyword pass.
Candidates came from scripts/youtube_channel.py sweeping the Met's own
channel search (234 distinct videos over 15 terms). ⚠ Those search counts
are page size, not relevance -- nearly every term returns a full ~30. Every
entry below was chosen by reading its title, and the two ambiguous ones
('This avant-garde French table...', 'Why do some call this table
seductive?') were resolved by reading their descriptions: a Lannuier card
table and an Oeben mechanical table respectively.
Titles, descriptions, dates and durations are NOT stored here -- they are
fetched from YouTube at ingest. Only OUR judgement lives in this file: which
videos, and how they are tagged. If the Met corrects a title, our card
follows on the next run; if we hand-copied it, it would not.
Tag vocabularies are the ones already in library_cards (period / form /
region / topic), read from the live table 2026-09-07. Do not invent new
terms here without adding them deliberately.
⚠ We embed and link. We never host, and we never take captions.

videos.teaser: Allan Breed turns and carves a Duncan Phyfe bedpost, filmed for the Met's 2011-12 Phyfe exhibition.
Allan Breed carves a bow knot and thunderbolt crest in low relief, in the Phyfe manner.
A close look at a Philadelphia table -- the questions a curator asks of a single piece.
Charles-Honoré Lannuier's pier table, in the Met's MetCollects series.
Curator Peter Kenny on a Lannuier card table -- French training arriving in New York.
American furniture reinstalled and reconsidered in the Met's American Wing.

Robert Laurent's carved chest, and the immigrant story behind it.
